items.title: "a protein switch that permanently alters gene expression ... (Vialou, et al, 2010)"
items.where: C. The "Hardened" Circuit: Dynorphin & DeltaFosB, P4
items.your_version: The Hardening: Chronic cycles lead to the accumulation of DeltaFosB, a protein switch that alters gene expression and holds the circuitry in place for weeks after the cycles stop ([Nestler, 2008](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2607320)). So the psychological trauma is reinforced biologically, which then reinforces the biology in a permanent loop until we make conscious efforts to break it from one or both ends.

items.title: Dynorphin and DeltaFosB read as partners here, and they aren't
items.where: C. The "Hardened" Circuit: Dynorphin & DeltaFosB, P1
items.your_version: The Problem: To protect itself from the Glutamate storm, the brain eventually releases Dynorphin, a chemical blanket that suppresses dopamine. This creates the "Void"--a state of apathy, grayness, and an inability to feel pleasure.

items.my_version: The Problem: To protect itself from the Glutamate storm, the brain eventually releases Dynorphin, a chemical blanket that suppresses dopamine. This creates the "Void"--a state of apathy, grayness, and an inability to feel pleasure. The two aren't one mechanism, though: DeltaFosB accumulates inside the dynorphin neurons themselves, and what it does there is turn dynorphin down, not up ([Zachariou, et al, 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16415864/)).

items.title: "the exact cocktail of catecholamines that transcribes new DeltaFosB proteins"
items.where: A. The Metabolic Red Line, P2
items.my_version: In this state, functional IQ drops substantially. More importantly, this state floods the Nucleus Accumbens with the catecholamines that transcribe new DeltaFosB proteins (the "armor"). The Takeaway: If you attempt to process trauma while living above this red line, you are not de-armoring; you are actively re-enforcing the armor.
